_readme: Source registry for scripts/generate-article.mjs.
EVERY URL BELOW IS UNVERIFIED. They are written from training data, which is
exactly the failure mode the playbook warns about: a model reconstructs the
SHAPE of a URL rather than recalling a real one. Some of these will be wrong.
Run `npm run check:feeds` before the first generation. It probes each one and
flips verified to true only on a live 200 with parseable items. The generator
refuses to use any feed still marked false, so a fabricated URL cannot reach
a published citation.
Only 404 and 410 mean dead. A 403 is a bot wall and a 5xx is a bad day —
both are recorded as unverified, not removed.
Each feed carries a jurisdiction. The generator writes the piece into that
silo, so a Fed item lands in /us/ and a BIS item in /general/. Add a feed
without a jurisdiction and it defaults to au.
NO FEED EXISTS FOR NEW ZEALAND OR INDIA.
Neither the RBNZ nor the RBI publishes an RSS feed. That is a fact about
those institutions, not a gap in this file, and no amount of guessing at
URLs will produce one. Those two silos need either a news source or a
different retrieval method before the generator can write for them.
FEEDS TAGGED jurisdiction: skip ARE NEVER USED BY THE GENERATOR.
The general silo requires a piece to compare two or more jurisdictions,
which a generator grounded in one feed item cannot do. Cross-border pieces
stay human-written. A BIS speech is cross-border in subject but it is still
one document, and one document is not a comparison.

feeds.note: Cross-border by nature. Tagged skip: see _readme on the general silo.
